text:
CONTROLLED FOLLOW-UP, replacing the diagnosis I retracted. This time every test varies ONE driver with everything else fixed, which is the discipline I failed at earlier on this bead.

WHAT IS NOW EXCLUDED BY MEASUREMENT. None of these produce anything close to 9 s/node:

  accumulation / leak     12 sequential calls: first-three mean 0.963 s, last-three 1.016 s,
                          ratio 1.05x, index-time correlation +0.084; RSS net MINUS 30 MB
  frame size              same node evaluated from frames of 320 / 160 / 40 / 10 nodes:
                          1.771 / 1.283 / 1.320 / 1.673 s - non-monotonic, 6 percent spread
  condition count q       q = 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 at fixed everything: 1.448 / 1.050 / 0.978 / 0.992 s
                          FLAT, despite D rising from 1 to 28 pairs
  support size            P=400, 12 nodes, radius varied so support goes 5.8 -> 71.8, a 12x rise:
                          1.180 / 0.603 / 0.829 / 0.653 s - cost FALLS
  feature count P         support held at 5.8, 12 nodes, P = 100 / 200 / 400 / 800:
                          0.688 / 0.786 / 0.866 / 0.842 s - only 1.22x across an 8x rise
  target policy           null 0.304 s vs plugin 0.195 s at q=8 - plugin is FASTER

At the closest synthetic match to the exemplar I could build - q = 8, P = 400, mean support 41,
a real compile_frame(searchlights(4.0)) - a sweep runs at 0.088 s/node. The exemplar reports
about 9 s/node. That is a factor of roughly one hundred, and none of the six analytic parameters
above accounts for any of it.

SO THE COST IS NOT IN THE COVARIANCE MATHEMATICS. Everything that determines the shape of the
Eq. 13 computation has been varied across its plausible range and none of it matters. That is a
large surface excluded, and it points the search at the data path instead: NIfTI-backed sources
and real block reads, the lm_relation_fit over real timeseries, or per-call source access that
synthetic in-memory matrices never exercise. Profiling one exemplar call would settle it in
minutes, and I cannot do that without the prepared Haxby data.

ONE SUBSTANTIVE DATUM ON THE PROPOSED FIX. The bead's first fix shape is a precompute-once object
shared across nodes. That mechanism appears to exist already as
residual_strategy = "shared_pair_statistics", documented as compiling reusable residual pair
sufficient statistics for a batch of overlapping supports. It IS reachable - on a real
compile_frame it runs; my earlier attempt was refused only because a hand-built additive_frame
carries no support index, and the message says so exactly:
"Shared pair statistics require a frame with an explicit support index."

But it does not pay off at these sizes:

  sweeping 1 node     node_local 0.404 s/node    shared_pair_statistics 0.764 s/node
  sweeping 10 nodes   node_local 0.088 s/node    shared_pair_statistics 0.162 s/node

Shared is about 1.8x SLOWER per node at both, so the amortization does not turn positive by ten
nodes. It may well turn positive at 577 nodes with 50-voxel spheres - that is exactly the regime
I cannot reach - but nobody should assume it will without measuring, and the fix the bead proposes
may already be implemented and simply not yet worth using.

Also worth noting because it is the opposite of the original hypothesis: per-node cost FALLS
sharply as a sweep proceeds here, 0.404 s at one node to 0.088 s across ten. Something is already
amortizing. The exemplar sees a flat 9 s/node over 577, so whatever amortizes in my setup does not
amortize there - another reason to suspect the data path rather than the algebra.

CAVEAT, stated plainly given my record on this bead. All of this is synthetic in-memory data. The
one thing I have established firmly is a negative: the analytic parameters do not explain the cost.
I am not offering a positive diagnosis this time.
